f.zone.central: Area A covers the largest cities. The cities in each area are listed in Annexure I of the Central wage order. If unsure, leave this: area C, the lowest rate, is used.
f.emp.permanent: Permanent job (government or regular, with increments)
f.occupation.help: Used to pick the minimum-wage category when income cannot be proved.
f.occupation.none: Not in this list, or not sure
f.monthlySalary.help: From the salary slip: basic pay, DA, HRA and other allowances. Leave out reimbursements such as travel or phone bills. Not the take-home amount.
f.monthlyTax.help: The income tax (TDS) shown on the salary slip. Leave empty and it is estimated from the tax slabs for that year.
f.itr: Income in the latest return before the accident (₹ a year)
f.claimed: Monthly income the family says they earned (₹)
f.claimed.help: Without documents, tribunals usually take the state minimum wage instead.
f.familyPension: Family pension now paid to the family (₹ a month)
f.spouse: Is the husband or wife claiming compensation?
f.dependentParents: Whether the parents depended on the person
f.cashless: Of which paid under the cashless treatment scheme (₹)
f.certificatePct: Permanent disability in the medical certificate (%)
f.basis.limb: One arm or leg, or one part of the body
res.range: Range, depending on unsettled points of law
res.rangeWide: The contested points move this a lot: read what could move it, below.
res.spread: Similar real awards: in {n} {kind} awards ({label}), half came to between about {a} and {b} for an estimate like this ({lo} to {hi} it). This reflects evidence and practice, not your legal entitlement.
res.head: Head
res.working: Working figures (not added to the total)

res.prove: What you will need to prove

res.interest.lead: Tribunals add simple interest from the date of filing, usually 6–9% a year. It is not in the number above.
res.cases.lead: Public judgments with similar facts, and what happened at each stage.
res.cases.none: No sufficiently similar case in the library yet.
res.cases.years: {y} years from accident to final amount
res.next.1: Free legal help: the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) in your district, or the NALSA helpline 15100.
res.next.2: Do not accept no-fault compensation (section 164) through the insurance company's settlement without advice: it ends the claim for full compensation.
res.next.3: Claims must be filed within six months of the accident; the Supreme Court has directed that, for now, claims should not be dismissed as late.
res.next.4: Advocates may not charge a percentage of the award.
res.offer: Check an insurance offer against this estimate
res.none.lead: On these facts the calculator cannot give a number. The reason is below.

offer.lead: An offer paid now is compared with the estimated award later, including interest, time and fees.
offer.years: Years until an award (if the offer is refused)
offer.interest: Interest the tribunal would add (% a year)
offer.discount: Value of money now vs later (% a year)
offer.fee: Fee a lawyer or agent would take, if any (% of the award)
offer.summary: The offer ({offer}) is {p}% of the estimate ({est}).

offer.caveat: Insurer offers in published Delhi awards were a median 9% of the final award, but those were offers families refused. Accepted offers are not published.
err.age: Enter the age in whole years, from 0 to 110.
err.number: Enter a number, like 6, or 0 if none.
err.amount: Enter rupees as a number, like 25000 or 2.5 lakh.
err.future: This date cannot be in the future.
err.beforeAccident: The claim cannot be filed before the accident.
err.cashless: Cannot be more than the medical bills.
elig.owner: An owner-driver hurt with no other vehicle involved has no third-party (section 166) claim. Check the vehicle's personal accident cover.
elig.unidentified: When the vehicle is not identified, compensation is claimed under the hit-and-run scheme (section 161), not through this estimate.
elig.s164: Accepting no-fault compensation through the insurance company's settlement ends the claim for full compensation (section 166).
res.cases.disclaimer: Real, public judgments. Every case turns on its own evidence: these show what happened, not what you will get.

warn.S164_LAPSES_166: The claim for full compensation has lapsed
warn.OWNER_DRIVER_NO_166: No third-party claim for an owner-driver
warn.LIMITATION: File the claim soon: over six months since the accident
warn.CONTRIBUTORY_NEGLIGENCE: Compensation may be reduced for the person's own negligence
warnmsg.AGE_OUTSIDE_TABLE: Age {age} is outside the Sarla Verma table; multiplier {multiplier} used.
warnmsg.NO_CERTIFICATE: No disability certificate given: loss of future earning capacity is taken as nil (except in the claimant's best case, when the person cannot work at all). Add the certificate's percentage when there is one.
warnmsg.FUNCTIONAL_ESTIMATED: No functional-disability assessment given; estimated from the disability certificate. Ask the doctor/board for a functional assessment.
warnmsg.S164_LAPSES_166: No-fault compensation (s.164) was accepted through the insurer's settlement. Under s.166(1) the claim petition lapses, so no further s.166 compensation can be estimated. Speak to the District Legal Services Authority (free).
warnmsg.OWNER_DRIVER_NO_166: An owner-driver hurt in a single-vehicle crash has no third-party (s.166) claim. Check the vehicle's personal accident cover instead.
warnmsg.UNIDENTIFIED_USE_HIT_AND_RUN: The offending vehicle is untraced: apply under the hit-and-run scheme (s.161): {death} for death, {hurt} for grievous hurt.
warnmsg.UNINSURED: The vehicle was uninsured: the owner/driver must pay, which is harder to recover. Seek legal aid early.
warnmsg.LIMITATION: More than {months} months since the accident. s.166(3) sets a 6-month limit, but the Supreme Court has directed (interim order, 4 Nov 2025) that claims not be dismissed as time-barred while it decides the challenge. File as soon as possible.
warnmsg.CONTRIBUTORY_NEGLIGENCE: The person was driving a vehicle involved in the crash: the tribunal may reduce compensation for contributory negligence.
warnmsg.RANGE_TOO_WIDE: The contested points move the amount a lot; see the scenario cards and swing factors rather than a single range.
warnmsg.INJURY_EXPERIMENTAL: Injury estimates are experimental: the non-pecuniary heads use bands calibrated on Delhi tribunal awards (2024-26) only, and are not yet legally signed off.
warnmsg.NOT_A_PREDICTION: This is the amount the Supreme Court's method gives on the facts entered — not a prediction of what a tribunal will award or when.
warnmsg.RULE_UNVERIFIED: Draft rules: not yet signed off by the legal reviewers.
warnmsg.ZONE_ASSUMED: No zone given for {state}; used {zone}. Choose the zone of the person's place of work.
warnmsg.MW_MISSING: No verified minimum wage for {state} on {date}. The estimate cannot be computed without it.
warnmsg.MW_MAY_BE_OUTDATED: The latest {state} minimum wage on file took effect on {from}, more than {months} months before the accident, and the official source has not been checked since the accident date. A later revision may apply.
warnmsg.MINOR_DEATH_CONTESTED: The income basis for a child's death is unsettled; the range shows both approaches.
warnmsg.TAX_ESTIMATED: Income tax estimated from FY {fy} slabs; enter actual TDS if known.
warnmsg.TAX_ESTIMATED.itr: Income tax estimated from FY {fy} slabs on the average return income.
warnmsg.TAX_YEAR_MISSING: No tax table for FY {fy}; used the latest table.
lim.MW_MISSING: This calculator does not yet have the official minimum wage for {state} on the accident date. For this type of work the estimate rests on that wage, so it cannot give a number yet. The claim itself is not affected: free legal help is available from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or the NALSA helpline 15100.

swing.under_15_multiplier: For a child under 15, courts use a multiplier of 15 or of 18
swing.bachelor_large_family: For an unmarried person supporting a large family, courts deduct a half or a third for personal expenses
swing.attendant_rate: An attendant's pay at the unskilled or the semi-skilled minimum wage
swing.minor_death_income: Courts differ on the income to use for a child's death
swing.non_earning_elderly: Courts differ on the income to use for an older person without a pension
swing.pension_basis: The pension lost: the full pension, or the pension less the family pension now paid
swing.spouse_only_deduction: When the husband or wife is the only dependant, courts deduct a half or a third for personal expenses
swing.conventional_escalation_steps: How many 10% increases are added to the fixed amounts (funeral, estate, consortium)
swing.functional_pct: How much of the earning capacity the injury takes, judged from the certificate
swing.non_pecuniary_band: Pain and suffering, amenities, conveyance, diet and attendant: amounts vary between tribunals
swing.itr_post_accident: Whether income tax returns filed after the accident are counted
swing.student_income: A student's income: the skilled minimum wage, or the amount in earlier cases for the course
swing.homemaker_income: A homemaker's work valued at ₹30,000 a month (Supreme Court, 2026) or at the minimum wage
swing.injured_homemaker_income: An injured homemaker's income: the minimum wage, or the Supreme Court's 2026 value by analogy
swing.mw_category: Which skill level of minimum wage the tribunal accepts for the occupation
res.parentsAssumed: Assumes the parents depended on the person. If they did not, about {d} less.

facts.title: Why this matters
fact.1.text: Crash claims waiting in court. 1 in 4 has waited more than 5 years.
fact.2.text: For every ₹1 the insurer offered, the court later awarded about ₹11. From 44 Delhi cases where families said no.
fact.3.text: Low-income families hit by a crash were not aware of any compensation scheme.
